summary: Iteration 27 (R7, hidden fields made visible). Backend: new pytest file with 16 tests: 14 pass, 1 fails (predicted XI has no goalkeeper), 1 fails as expected (follow_alerts ignores real SportAPI card/own-goal/penalty event types). One more bug, Insights missing usual_p, was found and fixed by the tester (one line). run_tests.sh self-tests all PASS, iter25 and iter26 regression 13 pass and 3 skipped, check-copy passed. Frontend (Playwright, desktop): forecast cards show the usual tick and '+N pts vs usual'; the 'Biggest rise vs usual' sort works; the forecast sheet shows the usual line, the last-10 strip for team and player, and Note -> Save note (persisted). The record line is correctly hidden because the track record is not ready (176/300). Search 'sa' shows 'Next NN%'. The Lineups tab shows a predicted eleven with 22 dots. Follow match works: Following state, You > Follows links to /match/{id}, the match appears in the feed and in the rail. The live-sheet momentum bar renders. Admin zones drawer: add, save, public table bands and legend, then remove, all verified. Player LaLiga rank card works. The Squad tab is first, with 24 cards and photos. Today and Insights date dots show. Account Lineup and Goal switches persist. Finder presets: local presets merge on sign-in, saved presets reach the account, and a second browser context sees them. Chosen leagues first works in Explore, Today, Search and Finder, but not in Insights. /admin home and the R5/R6 pages render.

critical.issue: The event filter is {type:'goal'} OR (type ~ /card/ AND extra ~ /red/). Stored SportAPI events use event_type names like red_card, second_yellow, own_goal and penalty (see the LiveBits WORD map), and extra_info holds the player name or 'Goal'. As a result, red cards, second yellows, own goals and penalty goals never trigger a goal_alert. Reproduced in test_follow_alerts_real_event_types: 0 of 4 alerts were sent. Fix: match type in {goal, own_goal, penalty} for goals and {red_card, second_yellow} for red cards, and set 'what' to match.

The Pro-only 'alerts' entitlement (default False, 'Part of Pro' in Welcome) is never checked. Any verified free user who follows a team, player or match gets lineup_alert and goal_alert e-mails. The Account > Notifications page also shows all three alert switches to free users without a Pro lock, which does not match Welcome step 3.

minor.issue: The engine makes no GK forecasts (distinct forecast pos = DEF/MID/FWD). So the predicted eleven always has 0 keepers and 11 outfield players, and the keeper area of the pitch is empty. The spec says 1 GK per side. Fill the GK from the players collection (most minutes or most starts) when no GK forecast exists.

FIXED BY TESTER: the feed did not call _usual(), so no card had usual_p, the Insights usual line was missing and 'Biggest rise vs usual' sorted nothing. Added _usual(db, fc) after the slice in insights_feed (queries.py).
vars={**vars, 'link': ... + vars.pop('path')} copies vars before the pop, so 'path' is also sent to the template. Harmless.
follow_alerts rows (_id 'lineup:{uid}:..', 'live:{uid}:..') are not removed when an account is deleted. Small privacy leftover.
pos uses $last without a $sort before $group, so the position shown is not deterministic for players who changed role.

ui_bugs.issue: favFirst compares f.league_iid (an integer iid) with prefs.leagues (league uuid ids), so chosen leagues are never moved first. Verified with prefs.leagues=[Premier League]: chips stayed LaLiga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Premier League. Explore put PL first. Fix: key by f.league?.id, or map ids to iids.
No goalkeeper dot (see the backend issue). The pitch shows 4-3-3 or 3-5-3 shapes with an empty keeper zone.

integration_issues.issue: The effect depends on the me.user object, which changes after every Finder run (/auth/me refetch). So GET /me/presets runs again after each search. In one run, a preset saved right after a search was missing from the chips (state was overwritten by the stale GET) while the API had it. It appeared after a reload. Use [me?.user?.id] as the dependency.
